boards.title: Your First Weekend at Simmons University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented on campus, connecting with student life, and exploring nearby arts spaces.

cards.title: Start with the Academic Quad
cards.subtitle: First stop — Main College Building, 300 The Fenway
cards.notes: Begin outside the Main College Building and use the academic quad as your landmark while you identify entrances, campus services, and routes between buildings.
cards.short_summary: Use the academic-campus hub to get your bearings.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons identifies 300 The Fenway as its Boston campus address and depicts the Main College Building on its campus map.
cards.source_title: Campus Tours and Information Sessions | Simmons University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor orientation stop; follow posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Set a Meet-Up Point at Common Grounds
cards.subtitle: Second stop — College Center, Main College Building
cards.notes: Choose a simple meeting point in Common Grounds, then use the nearby student computers and wireless area to coordinate the rest of the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A campus café stop with seating and nearby student resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons states that Common Grounds Cafe is in the College Center of the Main College Building and that its surrounding area has computers and free wireless access for students.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks are sold; confirm current hours and payment options before going.

cards.title: Reserve a Library Study Room
cards.subtitle: Third stop — University Library, 300 The Fenway
cards.notes: Book a group study room for a short planning session, browse the library spaces, and save the research-help links for your first assignments.
cards.short_summary: Turn a short library visit into a practical study-plan setup.
cards.evidence_claim: The Simmons University Library offers 20 group study rooms for student use, reservable up to 28 days ahead.
cards.access_notes: Study-room reservations and library access may require a Simmons account or ID.

cards.title: Find a Piece of Simmons History
cards.subtitle: Fourth stop — University Archives at the Library
cards.notes: Pause at the Archives exhibit in Lefavour Hall, then note one campus-history topic to revisit when you want context beyond the current semester.
cards.short_summary: Pair campus orientation with an archival history stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons University Library lists a University Archives exhibit on gender equality and LGBTQIA+ activism in Lefavour Hall, Level 1.
cards.access_notes: Exhibit availability can change; check with the library service desk if needed.

cards.title: See What Is Hanging at Trustman
cards.subtitle: Fifth stop — Main College Building, fourth floor
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition and take a quiet gallery lap; return for an artist talk or opening if the calendar lists one that fits your weekend.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery visit that works as a calm afternoon reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Trustman Art Gallery is in the Main College Building’s fourth floor and presents professional artists’ work plus an annual student exhibition.
cards.source_title: About the Trustman Gallery | Simmons University
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours listed by Simmons are Monday–Wednesday and Friday 10 a.m.–4:30 p.m., Thursday 10 a.m.–7 p.m.; verify exhibition dates before visiting.

cards.title: Locate a Backup Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Sixth stop — One Palace Road, Academic Campus
cards.notes: Use the building’s study map to find the lobby lounge and identify reservable private rooms, giving your group a backup place for a later work session.
cards.short_summary: Know where to go when you need a quieter campus base.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ One Palace Road study map identifies a lobby lounge and private study rooms, including one that must be reserved ahead.
cards.source_title: One Palace Road Study Map | Simmons University
cards.access_notes: Private-study-room use and after-hours access are subject to the building map’s instructions and reservation rules.

cards.title: Share a Meal at Bartol
cards.subtitle: Seventh stop — Residence Campus
cards.notes: Meet over a meal at Bartol, then compare classes, clubs, and plans for the week; choose options that work for your dietary needs before ordering.
cards.short_summary: A residence-campus meal stop built for catching up.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons describes Bartol Dining Hall as its all-you-care-to-eat dining facility on the residence campus, with vegetarian options, salad bars, sautés, pizza, and smoothies.
cards.access_notes: Dining is paid through an applicable meal plan or other offered payment option; check current menu and hours first.

cards.title: Take a Movement Break at Holmes
cards.subtitle: Eighth stop — 331 Brookline Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a low-key workout, lap swim, or indoor-track visit around your access privileges, then save the recreation schedule for future fitness classes.
cards.short_summary: A practical recreation stop on the Residence Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons identifies the Holmes Sports Center as a 60,000-square-foot facility with a swimming pool, cardio equipment, and hardwood courts for students and members.
cards.access_notes: Student or member access applies; verify facility and lap-swim availability before heading over.

cards.title: Use Your Simmons ID at the Gardner
cards.subtitle: Ninth stop — 25 Evans Way, beside the Academic Campus
cards.notes: Reserve a timed entry, bring your Simmons ID, and give yourself time to move through the galleries without treating the visit like a rushed checklist.
cards.short_summary: A nearby museum visit available to Simmons students with ID.
cards.evidence_claim: Simmons’ official Boston guide states that Simmons students receive free admission to the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum by showing their Simmons ID.
cards.source_title: The Official Simmons Guide to Boston | Simmons University
cards.access_notes: The museum recommends advanced timed tickets; bring a current Simmons ID for the stated free-admission benefit.

cards.title: Finish with Free Contemporary Art at MAAM
cards.subtitle: Tenth stop — 621 Huntington Avenue
cards.notes: Reserve a time slot, explore the current galleries, and end the weekend by discussing one work that caught your attention before heading back to campus.
cards.short_summary: A free contemporary-art stop near the Longwood Medical Green Line station.
cards.evidence_claim: MassArt Art Museum identifies itself as Boston’s only free museum of contemporary art and asks visitors to reserve tickets in advance.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; reserve in advance and check current open days before leaving campus.
